name: fend
why: A unit-aware arbitrary-precision calculator is a neat niche tool, but calculators are a crowded space with little that feels strange.

brief.what_it_is: fend is a command-line calculator, with a REPL and a web interface, that evaluates expressions with units attached. You type an expression such as "1 ft to cm" or "100 C to F" and it prints the result with its unit, for example "30.48 cm" or "210 °F". It works in exact rational numbers, so results are arbitrary-precision. It also handles complex numbers, number bases from 2 to 36, variables, D&D-style dice rolls and lambda calculus. It is published as a Rust crate, with an npm WASM build for use in other software.
brief.why_it_exists: The README gives no explicit motivation. It describes fend as an arbitrary-precision unit-aware calculator and lists its features as "Unique features".
brief.how_it_works: The README does not explain the internals. It says arithmetic uses rational numbers, which is how it stays arbitrary-precision, and that units are tracked through conversions such as "5'10" to cm". It also names a companion core library, fend-core, in a crates.io download badge.

commands_seen.context: Run with no arguments to start a REPL session, where you type expressions at the > prompt.

brief.install_notes: Packages are listed for Homebrew, MacPorts, AUR, AOSC OS, Void (xbps), Nix (nixpkgs.fend, or nix-shell -p fend), Cargo, winget, Chocolatey, Scoop and pkgx. Prebuilt binaries are on the GitHub releases page. No accounts, runtime or configuration are mentioned for the CLI. The README mentions a Telegram bot and npm WASM packages as alternative ways to use it.
brief.standout: Unit-aware calculation is combined with exact rational arithmetic, base conversion, complex numbers, dice rolls and lambda calculus in one small tool. Unit handling covers SI, US and UK customary units and many historical units.
brief.status: unknown. The README has a build CI badge and crates.io badges, and it lists many active package-manager entries, which suggests ongoing packaging. The README gives no release dates or changelog, and the GitHub page I fetched did not show a last-commit date, so I could not confirm recent activity.
brief.caveats: The README does not mention any warnings or known limitations. The homepage I fetched contained only a title and no content, so the details here come from the GitHub README. The manual lives at printfn.github.io/fend/documentation/, which I did not fetch. The scout note calls calculators a crowded space. The license is MIT.
